content: SQL is how you ask a database questions. SELECT picks columns, FROM picks a table, WHERE filters rows. JOIN combines tables that share a key. Always filter first in your mind: which rows, then which columns, then how to group them. Practice parameterized queries so user input cannot change the meaning of the command.

A REST API is a way for programs to exchange information over HTTP using resources and standard methods. Imagine a restaurant: the client is the customer, the API is the menu and waiter, and the server prepares the result. A URL identifies a resource, such as /books/42. GET reads it, POST creates something, PUT or PATCH updates it, and DELETE removes it. A request can include headers for metadata, a body for data (often JSON), and a method. The response includes a status code: 200 means success, 201 means created, 400 means the request was invalid, 401 means authentication is required, 404 means the resource was not found, and 500 means the server failed. For example, GET /books/42 might return JSON describing one book. REST APIs let a web page or mobile app use a service without needing to know how its server is implemented.

Pandas is a Python library for tables (DataFrames). Use read_csv to load data, head to peek, isna to find holes, groupby to summarize, and merge to join tables. Clean column names, check dtypes, and never assume a CSV is tidy. Matplotlib then turns those summaries into charts.

Mean is the balancing point, median resists outliers, and standard deviation describes spread. A hypothesis test asks whether a difference is likely just noise. Correlation is not causation. For careers, salary medians are more honest than means when a few high earners pull the average up.

A data analyst helps a team decide using evidence. Daily work is often SQL pulls, spreadsheet checks, dashboards, and explaining results to non-technical people. You do not need to invent new algorithms first. You need clean data, the right metric, and a sentence a manager can use.

A data scientist adds statistical and machine learning models on top of analysis. The job still starts with messy data and a business question. Models must be evaluated on unseen data. Communication matters as much as algorithms because a model nobody trusts will not be used.

A data engineer makes data reliable for everyone else. That means pipelines, warehouses, tests, and clear table design. If analysts cannot find trustworthy tables, models and dashboards fail. Think in terms of freshness, uniqueness, and documented grain of each table.

An AI engineer puts models into products: APIs, retrieval, evaluation, and monitoring. Large language models need constraints, citations, and tests. Easy explanations, safety, and cost control are part of the job, not extras.

Aerospace engineers apply physics to vehicles that fly. The work is conservative because failure is expensive and dangerous. CAD, analysis, testing, and documentation sit together. Programming (Python or MATLAB) is now a normal part of the toolkit.

Use your limited hours as a repeating loop: 1) a short review of yesterday, 2) one new concept with notes in your own words, 3) a tiny practice task, 4) a question you still cannot answer. Sleep and weekly review beat cramming. Projects lock skills in.

A good roadmap is not a pile of courses. It is a sequence of skills ordered by dependence, sized to your weekly hours, with projects as checkpoints. If you already worked in a nearby role, skip beginner repeats and spend time on the gap skills.

Projects should be small enough to finish and specific enough to show judgment. Pick a question, a dataset, a method, and an audience. Write what you would tell a hiring manager in six sentences. For computer science careers, shipping something beats collecting certificates.

Excel is a grid for thinking. Learn absolute vs relative references, PivotTables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and charts. Keep raw data on one sheet and analysis on another. When a file becomes fragile, that is a signal to move the same logic into SQL or Python.

Matplotlib draws charts from arrays. Start with a clear question: compare, trend, or distribution. Label axes, avoid 3D decoration, and use color with meaning. Cornsilk and navy palettes can still be readable if contrast is high.

Job market numbers in this app are educational estimates built from a dataset, not live job-board counts. Compare careers inside the same field. Look at median salary, openings index, 5-year growth, and remote share together rather than chasing the single highest salary.

If you have no job history, that is a valid starting point. Your education and hours available become the main inputs. The system will assume beginner skills and include extra foundation weeks. Portfolio projects then become your evidence.

When you change careers, the overlap with your current role is an asset. A data analyst moving to data science already has SQL and storytelling. Spend time on statistics and models. An engineer moving into data should keep domain knowledge and add analysis tools.
Passwords are stored as hashes, not as readable text. The profile page hides them behind dots. Changing a password requires the current one first so a borrowed session cannot silently reset it.
Your NorthStar ID looks like Interstellar-0000-0001. It is assigned in login order and never edited. Friends can find you with this ID the same way a database uses an autoincrement key.

When a lesson is confusing, ask for an analogy, a tiny example, then the formal definition. If you are stuck on a formula, plug in small numbers. If you are stuck on code, state the input, the error, and what you expected.

Do not invent data. Do not claim live salaries if you used a teaching dataset. For health and finance, respect privacy. For AI answers, treat the model as a tutor, not an authority, and verify important facts.
